international.title: Department for Work and Pensions takes services offline after ‘cyber incident’ – UK politics live
international.summary: The department is working with cyber security experts to restore services and limit disruption Good morning, and welcome to the UK politics live blog. The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) has taken some services offline this morning after what it described as a “cyber incident”. There is currently little information about which services have been affected by the incident or how long the disruption is expected to last, but the DWP said benefit and pension payments “will be paid as normal”. Nearly 100 Labour MPs have urged prime minister Andy Burnham to reject plans to approve drilling at the Rosebank oilfield, exposing deep divisions within the party over climate policy and energy security. Our policy editor, Kiran Stacey , has more in this report: MPs are due to consider a bill in the Commons today aimed at tackling strategic lawsuits against public participation, known by its acronym Slapps. It aims to protect whistleblowers, journalists, victims of sexual assault and others who speak out on matters of public interest from being silenced by costly or intimidating legal action brought by wealthy or powerful individuals and organisations. The bill, introduced by Conservative MP John Whittingdale, would make it easier for courts to dismiss such cases at an early stage. Continue reading...
